articleTitle: Connecting the Arts and Music to Science and Engineering: Burg inspiring creative students [Amperes: Current Affairs from Around the World]
abstract: By combining her passion for teaching, computer science, and art instead of choosing one over the other, Jennifer Burg inspires others and is creating better scientists and engineers. She provides a prime example of why it's great to tackle multiple efforts in one's career.

articleTitle: A Fulfilling Position: Villeneuve revolutionizing e-commerce [Amperes: Current Affairs from Around the World]
abstract: It's Orange Week at Kiva Systems, which means all the "newbies" hired over the course of the last quarter are spending the week getting to know each other and their new employer. Tomorrow there will be what COO and President Amy Villeneuve calls speed dating, where every new hire rotates through a series of rapid sit-downs with company executives. There is a LEGO Mindstorms robotics competition, a raffle challenge to further encourage networking, and a graduation party on Friday thrown by the previous class.

articleTitle: The Technology Ecosystem: Fueling Google's Chromecast [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: Imagine plugging a tiny device into your high-definition television (HDTV), connecting it to your Wi-Fi, and instantly sending videos, music, and more from any device-your smartphone, tablet, or laptop-all at the press of a button, and it just works. This is Google's Chromecast.

articleTitle: Given the Green Light: El-Tantawy driven by adaptive signal control [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: Samah El-Tantawy is cofounder and director of a yet-to-be-named start-up company in the adaptive traffic signal control industry. She completed her Ph.D. in 2012 in the field of intelligent transportation systems at the University of Toronto. She completed her bachelor's degree in electrical and communication engineering and her M.Sc. degree in engineering mathematics at Cairo University in 2004 and 2007, respectively.

articleTitle: A Master of Negotiation: Cozzo working to set new standards [Women to Watch]
abstract: Technology is all about innovation: every technical advancement seems to be newer, faster, or smarter than a previous version. But even innovation comes with rules.

articleTitle: Ensuring Your Opinions Are Valued: Tips for the Female Engineer [Career Advisor]
abstract: I have been a design engineer and a Registered Professional Engineer in Maryland and South Carolina for over 20 years. I started my career in an engineering firm right after I graduated with a bachelor's of science degree in electrical engineering. Over my career, I have risen through the ranks in the firm from entry-level engineer to electrical principal engineer, in charge of many other professionals. My work has taken me all over the United States designing projects such as power plants and new hospitals.

articleTitle: Building Communications: Agrawal spurs wireless research [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: In 2001, when wireless communications pioneer and Vodafone CEO Samuel Ginn gave US$25 million to Auburn University to establish the first wireless engineering degree program in the United States, the university asked Prathima Agrawal to come to Alabama to set up and run the new program. Thus, the new Wireless Engineering Research and Education Center (WEREC) emerged.

articleTitle: Grooming Future Engineers: All-girls robotics team thrives [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: A new robotics team at the all-girls high school at St. Mary's Academy (SMA) in Cherry Hills Village, Colorado, is making waves in the robotics community. The SMAbotics team attended its first competitions in 2013 and 2014 and did well enough to compete in regionals in its first year. The team had a mix of eight girls in its first year, mainly juniors and seniors, and at the beginning of the team's second year more than 20 with a wide range of interests will participate.

articleTitle: Good Vibrations: Schnitta Tackling Acoustical Engineering
abstract: When Bonnie Schnitta saw a video of the Tacoma Bridge in Washington state collapse due to vibrations caused by wind conditions, she knew she had "heard" her calling. "I remember sitting there watching this and thinking, 'I have no idea what field it is where you would learn why that happened, but one day that's what I'm going to do,'" she recalls. The field turned out to be acoustical engineering and, as founder and chief executive officer of SoundSense, Schnitta now tackles issues and applications of acoustics every day.

articleTitle: From Engineer to Mompreneur: Brooks progresses through the ranks [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: Careers in engineering offer many opportunities and open a variety of doors. I know this fact to be true firsthand. When it was time to select a career path, I was torn. I enjoyed writing, teaching, helping others, reporting, and solving problems. Choosing a career in engineering has given me the opportunity to experience all of my interests and more.

articleTitle: Orbiting Next-Gen Technology: The Women Behind Boeing's MexSat Satellite [Amperes: Current Affairs from Around the World]
abstract: In July 1963, Syncom, the world's first geosynchronous communications satellite, launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida. It was a month before Martin Luther King, Jr.'s march on Washington, D.C. Twenty-six-year-old Russian Valentina Tereshkova had just become the first woman to travel in space. The satellite, looking something like a table lamp with its conical base and shimmering shade, was used in the first live two-way satellite call between heads of government when U.S. President John F. Kennedy telephoned Nigerian Prime Minister Abubakar Balewa.

articleTitle: Life Lessons: Zaghloul has worn many hats [Women to Watch]
abstract: An electrical engineer by trade, Mona Zaghloul wears many hats and has an impressive resume including IEEE Fellow, professor, and director at George Washington University (GWU) and the National Science Foundation (NSF). Her work has spanned decades of projects in topics such as circuits and systems, microelectronics system design, very-large-scale integration circuit design, radio frequency microelectromechanical systems (RF-MEMS), neural networks, MEMS sensor systems, and biosensors and their interface circuit design. She views engineering as a rewarding career and hopes that many women will choose it.

articleTitle: Engineering an Opportunity: Romaniuk Fights for Her Dreams
abstract: If someone had told Antoanna Romaniuk 30 years ago that she'd one day work for a national government, she might have been skeptical. Involved with political dissidents as a student in the late 1970s and early 1980s, Romaniuk actively worked against the governments of Bulgaria and Poland to bring about political change, at one time finding herself stateless. Determined to create a better situation for herself and her family, Romaniuk took her life down a different path and now resides in the Maryland/Washington, D.C., area, working as a systems engineer on contracts with the U.S. Department of Defense.

articleTitle: DC Web Women: Helping women who work in tech [Career Advisor]
abstract: When the Internet took off in 1995, opportunities for coding and developing for the Web were numerous. Many women frequented Web sites, message boards, and forums geared toward Web development, but they had difficulty finding a place that would help them learn how to code and write for the Web.

articleTitle: Measuring the Effectiveness of Water Treatment Programs : Lantagne focusing on developing countries [Women to Watch]
abstract: In the mid-19th century, British doctor John Snow went against popular theory (the miasma theory, as it was called) when he deduced a connection between a London cholera epidemic and contaminated water. Snow had gone door to door mapping the outbreak until he finally narrowed the source to a well pump on London?s Broad Street. The handle was removed from the well pump, and today, if not then, that action is credited by some as ending the epidemic.

articleTitle: Inspiring the Underrepresented: Rosentrater is a role model, mentor, and teacher [Women to Watch]
abstract: Across the United States, females are grossly underrepresented as engineering graduates and professionals. A 2011 study by the American Society for Engineering found that women accounted for only 18% of undergraduate students in engineering. In the workforce it?s even lower. According to 2013 data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor and Statistics, women make up only 14.1% of the engineering workforce.

articleTitle: The Future of Malawi: President Joyce Banda has a Strong Vision of the Future
abstract: In 2009, Joyce Banda was elected Malawi?s first female vice president, but only months later she found her job in jeopardy when she refused to back the nomination of President Bingu Wa Mutharika?s brother Peter as successor of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP). Mutharika fired her as vice president of the DPP for ?anti-party? activities, but thankfully there was no impeachment. She continued to serve as the legal vicepresident of Malawi until 5 April 2012, when President Bingu Wa Mutharika suffered a fatal heart attack. When Mutharika?s cabinet sought to block Vice President Banda from becoming president, Army Commander Henry Odillo assured her of his support.

articleTitle: uwannadu Gets It Done: Providing a deeper look at potential careers [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: One of the most direct questions to ask a person is "What do you want to do?" But such a straightforward question does not always have an obvious answer, especially when it comes to career choices. Enter uwannadu.com, a new Web site that provides a discerning look at what a chosen career actually entails and links job options to relevant colleges and companies to offer a comprehensive look at particular career paths.

articleTitle: Humanitarian Efforts In India: Joint effort between IEEE groups offers hope [WIE from Around the World]
abstract: Getting to know Sarada Jayakrishnan, chair of the Kerala Section Women in Engineering (WIE) affinity group, was a chance to find out more about the region in which she grew up and why she decided to stay local and make a difference in her community. From the southernmost state of India, Jayakrishnan says she was lucky to grow up in Trivandrum, the capital of Kerala state. She completed her primary education there and went on to attend the College of Engineering in Trivandrum, graduating in 1991 with an electrical and electronics engineering degree.

articleTitle: A Perfect Union: Dahlberg educating "21st-century engineers" [Women to Watch]
abstract: Teresa Dahlberg experienced two monumental firsts in August of 2013: she relocated to New York City, and she took on her largest academic leadership responsibility yet, as dean of the Albert Nerken School of Engineering at The Cooper Union. But while the job and the city were new, she brought with her over 25 years of experience in engineering education and research as well as a long history of inspiring students to increase their participation with science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) fields, particularly in computer science and engineering.

articleTitle: Two Decades of WIE: Past Founders and Chairs Reflect on WIE's 20th Anniversary
abstract: IEEE Women in Engineering (WIE) is a unique organization in many ways, one of which being that it exists to serve the needs of the women who serve it as well; often the members who get the most out of WIE are those who have been actively involved. Most women will tell you that it is the entirety of everyone's efforts that have spurred the organization forward. Now, on the occasion of WIE's 20th anniversary, 12 women who were instrumental in bringing the group to the present day recall fond memories from the last two decades. These women, past founders and chairs, are the ones who led the community through the creation of the opportunities so many others enjoy, such as launching student affinity groups, funding awards, and editing the very magazine you are reading.

articleTitle: The Dynamic World of Cybersecurity: McMahon and Lockheed Offer New Solutions
abstract: Like a true engineer, Chandra McMahon has a formula for her career path: every time she takes on a new job, she examines the role to see if it will require 65% of her skills and offer 35% learning opportunity. "Doing this has resulted in my being able to stretch myself and take on roles where I thought I might not be capable," she explains. "It's enabled me to build my skills and keep growing."

articleTitle: Author and Educator: Shah follows her passion [Women to Watch]
abstract: Seema Shah is the (acting) principal at Vidyalankar Institute of Technology. She is also the dean of student affairs and an assistant professor in the Department of Information Technology at the institute. During an illustrious career spanning over 26 years, she has held senior teaching positions and has industrial experience as senior faculty at Patni Computer Systems. She has guided many projects at the postgraduate and undergraduate levels at a number of reputed institutes such as Veermata Jijabai Technological Institute, Don Bosco Institute of Technology, and Shreemati Nathibai Damodar Thackersey Womens University. Her subject expertise lies in grid computing, advanced operating systems, computer organization, data warehousing, distributed computing, and software testing, among others. Additionally, she has also conducted sessions on teaching methodology, microteaching, professional excellence, and interpersonal skills.

articleTitle: WIE did it together
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. As the IEEE Women in Engineering (WIE) 20th-year anniversary comes to a close, it gives me great pride to say that IEEE WIE is 'fabulous.' While this may be the end of the year-long celebrations, it doesn’t mean the energy, enthusiasm, and excitement ends. Your participation and dedication brought us this far and will continue to leave a legacy of excellence for years to come. Thank you for submitting pictures, videos, posters, and testimonials to celebrate this milestone. The passion about being a part of IEEE has been shown through the celebration submissions. Whether you are conducting humanitarian activities, pre-university outreach, networking events, teaching, and sharing information with others—you are creating a better tomorrow and making a difference! So, as this year ends, on behalf of IEEE WIE, I would like to say 'thank you' to all of the IEEE members, volunteers, staff, and supporters for making this an amazing and memorable year.

articleTitle: App-E-Feat
abstract: Advertisement: IEEE is launching a program that will connect IEEE members with organizations to develop mobile apps for the benefit of humanity. App-E-Feat will include a contest - sponsored by IEEE-USA - in which people will draw or develop an app to serve such efforts. Examples include apps that facilitate medical care, assistance after a natural disaster or increased food production. See http://www.appefeat.org.

abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members and society officers.

articleTitle: Thanks for 20 Wonderful Years of WIE!
abstract: Summary form only given. The IEEE Women in Engineering Program Manager would like to take this opportunity to thank all IEEE and Women in Engineering (WIE) Members, volunteers, and supporters for a wonderful 20 years! Our tremendous success would not have been possible without you. Your membership, activities, and dedication over the past two decades positioned WIE as a premier organization in support of women in science, technology, engineering, and math. Join us as we honor our past, treasure our present, and shape our bright future. Celebrate this milestone anniversary by submitting your individual or WIE event photos throughout the year. Submissions may be featured in our commemorative Global Faces of WIE e-book. Many thanks for all you do and for creating a dynamic and inspiring WIE community!

articleTitle: A Time for Reflection: Looking back on the accomplishments of 2013 [The Good, the Bad, & the Ugly: Engineering FACTS]
abstract: The start of the year is always one of reflection and planning. In reflecting on 2013, everything seems to have rushed by incredibly quickly. We ended the year with over 450 affinity groups that conducted 800+ inspirational outreach activities, engaging professional workshops, or advancing networking events around the world. I want to thank our wonderful 2013 IEEE Women in Engineering (WIE) Committee and global volunteers who helped us accomplish much and worked to lay a strong foundation of new initiatives. In planning for 2014, I welcome the energetic 2014 WIE volunteers who have committed to help shape the WIE program and expand our impact worldwide. Thank you for your continued engagement. I wish you the best as we celebrate WIE's 20th anniversary.

articleTitle: Lead beyond. Developing inspirational women who change the world
Engineers Week Is Right Around the Corner: Discover ways to make a difference all week long [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: U.S. National Engineers Week will once again bring together thousands of students and professionals, this year around the theme of "Let's Make a Difference." From 16 to 22 February, participants can get involved in activities around the country that benefit humanity, such as developing apps for charitable organizations or introducing children to science and technology through mentoring and setting up museum exhibits.

articleTitle: Fisher Earns Distinguished STEM Educator Award: Volunteering with IEEE helps balance life [Pipelining: Attractive Programs for Women]
abstract: During Engineers Week (Eweek), The Engineers' Council presented its annual Distinguished STEM Educator Award to highlight the most outstanding contributor helping raise awareness about technological literacy and interest in an engineering career. This year's winner, awarded in West Palm Beach, Florida, in February, was IEEE Member Dusty Fisher.

articleTitle: IEEE-USA Awards
abstract: Nominate a Colleague: Remember how great it felt to be recognized for an achievement or to witness someone you admire receive recognition for their effort? Now is the time to nominate deserving individuals for one of the prestigious IEEEUSA Awards. Nominations are being accepted until 31 July 2014.

articleTitle: Jones Earns Diversity Award: STEM outreach is saving the world [Women to Watch]
abstract: Pamela Jones, an IEEE Women in Engineering member and IEEE-USA Awards Board chair, recently won the Diversity Award at the 2013 Women of Color STEM Conference in October in Dallas, Texas. Jones was selected from a nationwide pool of private industry and government employees. The award celebrates her record of community service. Although Jones says she is honored and humbled to receive the award, she finds it a bit strange to ?get an award for something we all should be doing.
